programme.title: F1's Fiercest Rivalries with Karun Chandhok
programme.desc: From the personal insults of Nigel Mansell vs Nelson Piquet, the short but fiery feud between Ayrton Senna and Michael Schumacher, to a friendship turned sour between Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton, they’re all featured here. But what pair takes the Number 1 spot? Autosport Editor-In-Chief Kevin Turner sits down with former driver and Sky Sports F1 broadcaster Karun Chandhok to debate who they think are the Top 10 greatest rivalries in the sport’s 75-year history. Let us know who you think F1’s greatest rivalry was in the comments, and check back soon for a new series of F1 Top 10 Podcasts!

programme.title: How chaos ultimately decided the final podium lineup - F1 British GP Review
programme.desc: The British Grand Prix didn’t disappoint, with a dream victory for Lando Norris, beating teammate Oscar Piastri after the Australian picked up a 10-second penalty for erratic driving behind the Safety Car. But the star of the show was Sauber’s Nico Hulkenberg, who after 15 years and 239 starts in Formula 1, finally got his first podium finish. Autosport Editor-In-Chief Kevin Turner sits down with Jake Boxall-Legge and Ronald Vording to discuss all the action and news from Silverstone. Including Hulk's "incredible" podium, whether Piastri should have been penalised, Max Verstappen's spin from second and the persistent rumours over his future, and Mohammed Ben Sulayem's challenger for FIA President, Tim Mayer.

programme.title: F1 Rubber Stamps GM’s F1 Entry
programme.desc: So, after several years of preparations, negotiations, public arguments, and even the US Department of Justice getting involved, Cadillac has finally been formally announced as Formula 1’s 11th team for the 2026 season! Today’s formal announcement confirms the handshake agreement that the sport had with General Motors last November. After a revised bid led by Dan Towriss of the TWG Group (Formerly Andretti) was accepted. The Silverstone-based project now has the green light to prepare for its first race in just 12 months as a customer team with Ferrari power units until General Motors builds its own version for 2028. Motorsport.Com’s Editor in Chief, Ben Hunt, reacts to this breaking news, with Laitta Chemelo, Editor at Motorsport.Com and Nascar Reporter at Motorsport.com, Nick DeGroot.

programme.title: Michael Schumacher at Le Mans
programme.desc: In 1991, before his stellar F1 career, Michael Schumacher raced for Mercedes at Le Mans - and had a legitimate shot at winning the most prestigious endurance race in the World. Autosport Editor-in-Chief Kevin Turner narrates the story of this dramatic race, and explains how the lessons Schumacher learnt in these 900bhp cars shaped his career in F1, and assisted him in some of his most famous races.

programme.title: The car so good it shocked Ferrari
programme.desc: Ferrari dominated the 2004 F1 season, crushing its underachieving opposition and wrapping up both world championships early. It achieved that with a car that was so good from the moment it hit the track, that the team was convinced it had done something wrong. In this video we tell the story of how Ferrari tried to get to the bottom of what had gone wrong with the build of the car, while drivers Michael Schumacher and Rubens Barrichello were convinced the pace was real.

programme.title: Episode 5: Monster Jam and Rally Jameel
programme.desc: Gearing Up is back with another thrilling episode that takes you on an exhilarating journey around the globe, showcasing the most unique and intense competitions the world has to offer. In this episode, high skills, a passion for technology, an impatience for innovation, and a pure love for adrenaline are combined at their best. Buckle up, rev your engines, and get ready for some electrifying action as you experience the thrill of full G-force! The episode kicks off with Monster Jam’s action. Monster Jam drivers are the best of the best. They make 6-ton Monster Jam trucks defy gravity and wow fans around the world. Each driver has a signature stunt they can’t wait to perform during the event. In this episode, some of Monster Jam’s most technical drivers will break down their favourite skills. Then we go to Rally Jameel. As the first women-only navigational rally in the Middle East, it has returned with its highly anticipated fourth edition and its first-ever cross-border expansion. Spanning five days and covering a 1,600-kilometer route across two countries, this year’s rally represents a historic expansion beyond Saudi Arabia, as everything would start from Petra, Jordan. Lastly, finish off this episode by featuring the WaterJet World Series, one of the premier international jet ski racing competitions, typically consisting of several rounds held in different countries and continents.

programme.title: What Horner's sacking really means for Verstappen, F1 and Red Bull
programme.desc: After 20 years of service as Team Principal of Red Bull Racing, Christian Horner has been sacked by the team with immediate effect, with Laurent Meikes replacing Horner as Red Bull CEO, and Alan Permane taking Meikes’ job as Racing Bulls Team Principal. James Allen is joined in the studio to analyse the news with our correspondents Ronald Vording, Christian Nimmervoll and Ben Hunt to analyse what led to Horner’s sacking, what role Max Verstappen and his camp may have played in the decision, and what it means for Red Bull, Racing Bulls, and maybe even Ferrari in the future…

programme.title: Which of Marc Marquez's MotoGP victories make him a future racing legend?
programme.desc: Marc Márquez is widely considered one of the greatest motorcycle racers of all time, he previously raced for the Ducati satellite team Gresini in 2024 and Honda's factory team from his MotoGP debut in 2013 until 2023. At present he races for the Ducati Lenovo Team and is predicted to win the MotoGP Championship this year. Hearing from his past and present team, we learn all the stories from behind the scenes. From photoshoots, injuries, mistakes and laughs, let's look back on Marquez's greatest races so far.

programme.title: 1000 Lakes Rally 1986
programme.desc: The Italian Lancia and the French Peugeot teams came to the renowned 1000 Lakes Rally hotly disputing the manufacturers' title, with Markku Alen matched against Timo Salonen. Peugeot, however, had another ace in the pack in the shape of 27 year-old rising local star Juha Kankkunen, who was looking extremely good for the drivers' championship. This video captures in enthralling fashion the red-hot battle through the Finnish forests, with their huge ‘yumps’ and flat-out straights. Always a rally to set the pulses racing, Alen had the Lancia Delta running at its best and his ability to control the S4 at seemingly impossible speeds and angles will amaze the viewer. Supporting him would be Kalle Grundel, specially released from his Ford RS200 commitments and pushing hard on his home territory. Again though, Peugeot were taking no chances by fielding the experienced Stig Blomqvist, also no stranger to the 1000 Lakes
